name: 45759-shortprompt-qwen3600m-1gpu
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, `--gres=gpu:1`), sm90. Prefer an idle node: the quantity is a few milliseconds of host time, so CPU contention moves it more than the GPU does.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1 -- one engine, one GPU. `--api-server-count` left at the engine's own default of 1.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=1, bounded at 2000 requests with a 900 s safety cap, first 10% warmup and last 10% cooldown by completion, leaving 1600 measured.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets: prompt exactly 16 tokens, output exactly 8, sent to `/v1/completions` with `ignore_eos: true` and `temperature: 0`, streaming on. Three of those are load-bearing rather than incidental. `/v1/completions` is part of the declaration -- a run against `/v1/chat/completions` is a different setup and will complete without error. Streaming stays on and the output stays longer than one token, because guidellm stamps a first-token boundary only when a later token follows the first: a 1-token output records no TTFT on any request and the metric silently reads 0.0, and `ignore_eos: true` is what keeps every request reaching 8. Prompt length is exact -- a BOS token cancels against the count, so `prompt_tokens: 16` reaches the engine as 16.
purpose: A single-user autocomplete service on one small Qwen model and one GPU, answering 16-token prompts one at a time.
launch:
# The engine's command line: a stock single-GPU serve, nothing here is tuned. Host, port and
# served-model-name are not part of the declaration.
model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
tensor-parallel-size: 1
# Neither of these can bind at this workload's 24-token requests; they keep the KV pool small.
max-model-len: 1024
# 0.30, NOT the 0.80 this otherwise-verbatim serve line came with, and the reason is the shared
# card rather than anything about the workload. `request_memory` compares FREE memory against
# `util * TOTAL`, so 0.80 is a demand for 63.35 of 79.19 GiB and any neighbour holding more than
# a fifth of the GPU fails bring-up outright -- which is what happened on 2026-08-23: the
# harness reaped the card clean and read 81090 MiB free, then a third party took ~19 GiB during
# startup and the engine exited with "Free memory on device cuda:0 (59.82/79.19 GiB) on startup
# is less than desired GPU memory utilization (0.8, 63.35 GiB)".
#
# It cannot bind at 0.30 either, which is why lowering it is free. The whole working set is
# 1.2 GB of bf16 weights plus a KV pool for ONE 1024-token sequence: Qwen3-0.6B has 28 layers
# and 8 KV heads x 128, so K+V is 2 x 28 x 1024 x 2 B = 112 KiB per token, i.e. ~115 MiB for a
# full 1024-token context. 0.30 x 79.19 = 23.8 GiB is still ~17x the entire requirement, and it
# tolerates a neighbour sitting on 55 GiB.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.30
